title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E04 — Persecution and Saints
The Christian church catches the attention of the Roman emperor; he views the faithful as a threat to imperial authority and Roman culture; the widespread persecution of Christians that follows; a new class of Christian heroes, the martyred saints.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E05 — Peace between Empire and Church
In 312 A.D., Christianity gains a powerful ally when the Roman emperor Constantine adopts the faith of Jesus as his own; seeing how this shift affects Christian believers; the church goes from being a persecuted minority to a privileged minority.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E01 — Biblical Israel - The Story of a People
Entering the world of biblical Israel with a historical overview; an examination of how the Bible gives insights into the daily life of ancient Israelites; considering the context for how the Bible comes into being.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E02 — By the Rivers of Babylon - Exile
A look at the Babylonian exile; the exiled Judeans begin asking themselves who they are as a people and why they are conquered; as the Bible begins to be compiled in this time of exile, it offers two vantage points for understanding its history.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E03 — Ancestor Narratives in Genesis
Surveying the stories of ancient Israel's origins as preserved in the Book of Genesis; these origin stories are crucial for understanding the books that follow because ancient Israel understands itself to be a family that descends from Jacob.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E04 — Moses - The Torah's Central Hero
A look at Moses; the story of the Israelites' exodus from Egypt; tracing the narrative of Moses's journey, which includes receiving the Ten Commandments from Yahweh; reviewing the Torah, the "law of Moses"; the origins of the priesthood.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E01 — The Land of Canaan
What is meant by "holy land"; the difference between archeology and history; how reliable the Hebrew Bible is as a window into life in ancient Israel; answers to these and other questions; the region's earliest recorded inhabitants, the Canaanites.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E02 — The Arrival of the Israelites
What archeologists uncover about the arrival of the Israelites into Canaan; an ancient Egyptian stele with the earliest reference to Israel; the remains of Jericho's walls; a Philistine temple similar to the one Samson destroys in the book of Judges.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E03 — Jerusalem - An Introduction to the City
Surveying the topography and layout of Jerusalem; reviewing biblical accounts of Jerusalem from the arrival of David around 1,000 B.C.E. to the start of the Babylonian exile in 586 B.C.E.; the remains of an Assyrian siege on the city of Lachish.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E04 — The Jerusalem of David and Solomon
A first look at the biblical City of David; combing through the remains of a scribe's house behind a city wall; the development of biblical Hebrew script; rare examples of this script in a clay sealing, a piece of pottery and a victory stele.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E05 — Biblical Jerusalem's Ancient Water Systems
The City of David's ancient water system centered on the Gihon Spring; the three different water systems that are created due to the spring's location outside the city walls; these include Warren's Shaft, Siloam Channel and Hezekiah's Tunnel.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E06 — Samaria and the Northern Kingdom of Israel
Learning about Israel as it is ruled under the Omride dynasty between Solomon's death and the Assyrian invasion in 722 B.C.E.; exploring ruins such as the High Place at Dan; the acropolis at Samaria, which holds the remains of King Ahab's palace.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E07 — Fortifications and Cult Practices
Aspects of everyday life in the kingdoms of ancient Israel; how recessed gates are designed to protect cities from enemies; how altars, amulets, painted figures and pottery vessels reflect the religious beliefs at Kuntillet Ajrud and other sites.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E01 — From Jesus to the Creation of the Church
In the early days of the Christian faith, there is no church; no single institution to guide the followers of Jesus; stepping into the world of the early church; the roots of Christianity as found in ancient Jewish traditions and the gospel.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E02 — The First Christian Institutions
In the first century A.D., the followers of Christ evolve from a band of disciples into tight-knit communities of worship; a glimpse of these communities in some of the earliest Christian documents; the Acts of the Apostles and the letters of Paul.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E03 — Christianities in the Early Church
Christianity quickly spreads all over the Mediterranean region in the first few centuries; learning how believers adapt the practice of their faith to create a great diversity of worship in the early church.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E04 — Persecution and Saints
The Christian church catches the attention of the Roman emperor; he views the faithful as a threat to imperial authority and Roman culture; the widespread persecution of Christians that follows; a new class of Christian heroes, the martyred saints.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E01 — The Century's Initial Catastrophe
The opening lecture presents the main themes of the course; beginning with the concept of total war; other themes include the role of ideology, the meanings ascribed to the war by different sides and the war's legacy.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E02 — Europe in 1914
Examining the state of Europe and the world before the onset of the war in 1914; the emergence of the German Empire creates strains in the international balance of power; divided among Great Britain, France, Germany, Austria-Hungary and Russia.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E03 — Towards Crisis in Politics and Culture
Even among those who expect war, there are widespread misconceptions about the nature of the conflict to come; in this lecture, exploring the prevailing ideas and attitudes in Europe; the premonitions noted by contemporaries of coming disaster.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E04 — Causes of the War and the July Crisis, 1914
This lecture analyzes the immediate events that lead to war; the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary at Sarajevo in June 1914; the diplomatic chain reactions that follow in the July Crisis.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E05 — The August Madness
The hysterical celebration known as the August Madness greets the outbreak of war between the Central Powers (Germany and Austria-Hungary) and the Allies (France, Great Britain and Russia); how widespread this emotional outburst really is.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E06 — The Failed Gambles - War Plans Break Down
This lecture follows the unfolding of the German Schlieffen Plan, which envisions quick victory on two fronts; the French Plan XVII aims to recover lost French territories; both attempts are thwarted.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E07 — The Western Front Experience
The Western Front soon freezes into static trench warfare and horrific slaughter from attempts to break this deadlock; generals on both sides seek a breakthrough that allows sweeping offensives and glorious cavalry charges; these never materialize.

title: World War I: The "Great War"
description:
S01 E08 — Life and Death in the Trenches
A detailed overview of the trench landscape from the perspective of ordinary soldiers; the elaborate fortifications; the omnipresence of death; the codes of behavior such as the Christmas fraternizations between the trenches in 1914.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E01 — Hitler and the Nazi Youth
The horrors of Nazi Germany are one hallmark of World War II; pondering how ordinary German citizens find themselves participating in such heinous events; going inside the propaganda machine of Hitler's Germany; seeing how it targets the youth.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E02 — Japanese Soldiers in Nanjing
The origins of World War II lie in Asia in 1931; tracing the invasion of 1937 and the Rape of Nanjing; witnessing the events through the eyes of a Chinese soldier and a Japanese journalist, young men who bear witness to the flesh and blood of battle.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E03 — Panzer Leaders Who Changed Warfare
In addition to the story of people, World War II is the story of technology; perhaps nowhere is this more apparent than the tanks Germany uses to barrel across Poland and France in "lightning warfare"; how new technology defeats the old ways of war.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E04 — Jews Inside the Warsaw Ghetto
Wartime Warsaw offers a gateway to the darkest events of the war; bearing witness as the city's Jews are rounded up and put in the ghetto, where the specter of disease and starvation always looms; stories from several of the ghetto's inhabitants.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E05 — The Small Acts of the French Resistance
In Nazi-occupied France, informants create an environment of paranoia and fear, yet some people offer resistance in ways big and small; revisiting the legacy of the French Resistance to experience life under the Nazi boot.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E06 — A Child and a Pilot in the London Blitz
Shifting one's attention across the English Channel, where Britain faces the Nazi war machine alone; tracing the war in London through the eyes of a Jewish child in the East End, a bureaucrat performing unglamorous duties and a young Oxford student.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E07 — The Besieged at Leningrad
When the Nazis set up a siege of Leningrad in 1941, none of the city's inhabitants can envision the impact; finding out what daily life is like inside "the Ring" of besieged Leningrad through the eyes and diaries of three unforgettable women.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E08 — The Captured and Pursued in the Philippines
Prior to the war, Americans in the Philippines live in a "soldier's paradise"; this changes when the Japanese invade the country; seeing what life is like after the fall of the Philippines, from the Bataan Death March to an internment camp in Manila.
